stem:
Zaid rubs a plastic comb on dry hair and holds it near tiny paper pieces; the pieces jump to the comb. He rubs a second comb the same way and brings the two charged combs near each other.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The two charged combs repel because they carry like charges.
The two charged combs attract because they carry like charges.
The paper sticks to the comb even if the combs were never rubbed.
Like-charge repulsion applies only to combs, not to any other rubbed objects.

teacher.key_rationale: Like charges on the two rubbed combs repel. Attraction for like charges reverses the rule. Saying paper sticks with no rubbing drops the charge-by-rubbing condition. Limiting like-charge repulsion to combs alone over-narrows the rule.

mx_swap.reason: Sibling-term swap for static charge invents a neighbouring label not in the stem; kept relationship_reversal, condition_omission, and scope_error on the charge interaction.
